query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys have reported densities of 1.46–6 g/cm3 and commonly contain solid solutions together with intermetallic compounds. Earlier induction-melted Al–Mg-rich alloys established this structural complexity but did not resolve subsequent transformation pathways. Compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd alloys showed region-dependent compression and corrosion performance, while studies of AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys associated Mg content with phase stability and multiple functional properties. Most prior work emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, leaving corrosion, high-temperature oxidation, and evolution from metastable states comparatively underexplored. Within the design constraint of density below 6 g/cm3 and the tendency for constituent-property differences to promote stable intermetallic compounds, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain how a non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy evolves and why that evolution changes its corrosion and high-temperature oxidation behavior? Specify an unnamed controlled comparison, predictions relative to the initial baseline, boundary conditions, supporting prior observations, and an outcome that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.boundary: Alloy density below 6 g/cm3, Mg content above 10 at.%

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermally annealed alloy shows no significant improvement in corrosion resistance or reduction in high-temperature oxidation rate compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys has focused on understanding their microstructure, mechanical properties, and high-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier studies have explored the effects of composition, processing, and testing conditions on these properties. However, the evolution of non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys and their corrosion and high-temperature oxidation behavior remain underexplored.
decision.unsolved: The transformation pathways and evolution from metastable states in Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys are not well understood, and the relationship between their microstructure and corrosion and high-temperature oxidation behavior is still unclear.
decision.lever: in situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction and corrosion testing
decision.why: To investigate the time-temperature-dependent oxidation mechanisms and phase transformations of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and to understand how these transformations affect their corrosion and high-temperature oxidation behavior. This approach will allow for the identification of the key factors controlling the evolution of these alloys and the development of a mechanistic hypothesis to explain their behavior.
